purpose: Separate authoritative current grant definitions from historical Catholic customs, with precise work/occasion/conditions and no grant attribution by resemblance.

source_scope.primary_edition: 1999 fourth edition, web-hosted by Holy See

conditions_en: Perform the precise indulgenced work with the requisite devout disposition
Have at least the general intention to gain the indulgence and perform the prescribed work in the required manner and time
Be baptized, not excommunicated, in the state of grace at least at the end of the prescribed work, and—specifically for a plenary indulgence—have complete detachment from all sin, even venial sin
Prayer for the intentions of the Supreme Pontiff
general_plenary_conditions.temporal_note_en: The three sacramental/prayer conditions may be fulfilled on days before or after the work; Communion and prayer for the Pope's intentions are fittingly made on the day of the indulgenced work. See the norms for detailed application.
general_plenary_conditions.frequency_note_en: Ordinarily one plenary indulgence per day, apart from the exception at the point of death; one sacramental confession may serve several plenary indulgences but each plenary indulgence requires its own Communion and prayer for the Pope's intentions.
general_plenary_conditions.incomplete_conditions_note_en: If the required complete disposition or plenary conditions are lacking, the grant may be partial under Norm N.7, subject to the other norms and exceptions.
general_plenary_conditions.citation_correction: The previous reference to Norms 7–10 was erroneous: those norms primarily discuss diocesan/eparchial competence. The ordinary plenary conditions, eligibility, and frequency are set out in Norms 17–20.

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly recite the stanzas of Tantum ergo during solemn reposition of the Most Blessed Sacrament after the Mass of the Lord's Supper
special_conditions: Solemn reposition after the Mass in Cena Domini; mere visits to altars of repose do not constitute this specific prescribed work

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly take part in a solemn Eucharistic procession, whether inside or outside a church
grants.occasion_or_frequency: When a genuine solemn Eucharistic procession occurs; particularly Corpus Christi
special_conditions: Floral carpets and devotional decorations are not in themselves the specified participation

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly visit a cemetery and pray, even mentally, for the departed
special_conditions: The place must be a cemetery and the prayer must be for the departed

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly visit a church or oratory and recite the Our Father and Creed there
grants.occasion_or_frequency: All Souls' Day, or an authorised substitute day under the Ordinary's consent
special_conditions: Prescribed church/oratory visit and both prayers; a generic All Souls prayer is insufficient

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly visit a parish church and there recite the Our Father and Creed
grants.title_en: Parish church feast or Portiuncula visit
grants.occasion_or_frequency: Titular solemnity of the parish church or 2 August
special_conditions: The grant applies to the qualifying parish church visit, not merely a village fair, patronal procession or local celebration

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly visit a shrine constituted by competent ecclesiastical authority, and there recite the Our Father and Creed
grants.occasion_or_frequency: The shrine's titular solemnity; once in a year on a chosen day; or on a group pilgrimage
special_conditions: Official shrine status and one of the specific occasions must be established; not any destination bearing a religious name

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly participate in solemn singing or recitation of Veni Creator in a church or oratory
grants.title_en: Veni Creator on 1 January or Pentecost
special_conditions: Public solemn recitation or singing in church/oratory; a private casual recitation is not the specified plenary work

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly participate in solemn singing or recitation of the Te Deum in a church or oratory, giving thanks for the year's benefits
special_conditions: Public solemn recitation or singing in church/oratory, with thanksgiving purpose

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly visit the Most Blessed Sacrament to adore for at least half an hour
grants.title_en: Eucharistic adoration for half an hour
special_conditions: A mere church visit or tour does not fulfil the specified work

grants.prescribed_work_en: Members of the family devoutly recite an approved prayer before an image of the Sacred Heart or Holy Family on the day the family is first consecrated
grants.title_en: First family consecration to Sacred Heart or Holy Family
grants.occasion_or_frequency: Day of the family's first consecration
special_conditions: Priest or deacon conducts the rite if possible; not every family enthronement or later renewal is the first consecration
Members of the family are the specified beneficiaries

grants.prescribed_work_en: The anniversary observance described in the family consecration concession
special_conditions: Do not call an anniversary plenary on the basis of the first consecration grant

grants.prescribed_work_en: Publicly recite Iesu dulcissime, Redemptor, the act of dedication of mankind to Christ the King
grants.title_en: Public Christ the King act of dedication
grants.occasion_or_frequency: Solemnity of Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
special_conditions: The same act receives a partial indulgence in other circumstances
The difference between the 1999 law's Christ the King solemnity and the 1962 calendar date must be resolved, not assumed

grants.prescribed_work_en: Publicly recite Iesu dulcissime, the Sacred Heart act of reparation
grants.title_en: Public Sacred Heart act of reparation
grants.occasion_or_frequency: Solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
special_conditions: The public act on the solemnity is specified; private recitation in other circumstances is partial, not this plenary grant

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly take part in the adoration of the Cross during the solemn Good Friday liturgical action
grants.title_en: Good Friday veneration of the Cross
special_conditions: A privately held devotional crucifix or self-directed ceremony is not automatically the prescribed liturgical action

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly make the Stations of the Cross at legitimately erected Stations, meditating on the Passion and death of Christ
special_conditions: Fourteen properly erected crosses are required; movement from station to station, or the leader alone moving where a congregation cannot, under the specified provisions
Source also sets out approved alternatives for legitimately impeded faithful

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly recite at least five continuous decades of the Rosary with meditation on the mysteries in a church/oratory, family, religious community, association, or assembled group
grants.title_en: Five-decade Rosary in church, family or group
special_conditions: Five decades must be continuous and mysteries meditated upon
Public recitation must announce the mysteries according to approved local practice; other settings may receive partial indulgence

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly take part in an approved public novena exercise
grants.occasion_or_frequency: When the public novena is held
special_conditions: A family custom mentioning nine days is not by itself evidence of an approved publicly celebrated novena

grants.prescribed_work_en: Renew baptismal promises with an approved formula during the Easter Vigil celebration or on the anniversary of one's Baptism
special_conditions: A general seasonal custom is not an automatic act of baptismal renewal

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly recite Angelus with its versicles and prayer at dawn, noon or evening, or Regina caeli and the customary prayer during Easter time
grants.occasion_or_frequency: Daily at the customary hours; Regina caeli in Easter time
special_conditions: Relevant to Pray's existing Angelus reader, not to generic Marian decoration customs

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly visit a cemetery and pray, even mentally, for the departed
grants.title_en: Cemetery prayer for deceased outside plenary period
grants.occasion_or_frequency: Any day, with the plenary provision separately specified for 1–8 November
special_conditions: This concession is applicable only to the souls in Purgatory

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly recite the invocation Requiem aeternam, or Lauds or Vespers of the Office of the Dead
special_conditions: The concession is applied only to souls in Purgatory; exact devotional work, not all prayers for the dead

grants.prescribed_work_en: Devoutly use a cross, crucifix, rosary, scapular or medal duly blessed by a priest or deacon
grants.title_en: Devout use of blessed devotional objects
special_conditions: The named objects do not include every blessed household item, candle, palm or vessel; do not generalise

grants.prescribed_work_en: On the saint's calendar memorial, devoutly say a prayer in the saint's honour taken from the Missal or otherwise lawfully approved
grants.title_en: Prayer on a saint's calendar memorial
grants.occasion_or_frequency: On the saint's memorial as registered by the relevant calendar
special_conditions: A patronal fair or name-day gift alone is not the prescribed prayer

notes: The first-nine base remains and previous general-norm citation was corrected to Norms 17–20.
This registry is a source-verified 1999 concession seed, not a complete certification of later temporary/local 2026 decrees.
Current liturgical grant feast day cannot automatically be mapped to a 1962 feast date where solemnity classification or transfer differs.
Partial grants do not require the three ordinary plenary conditions, but the work, intention and basic eligibility still matter.
